title: Pruner: A Draft-then-Verify Exploration Mechanism to Accelerate Tensor Program Tuning
problem: Search-based tensor program tuning for deep neural network deployment is slow because the exploration mechanism applies an accurate-but-slow learned cost model to all candidate schedules, taking hours or days to find optimal programs. Additionally, learned cost models trained on one hardware platform cannot adapt online to a new platform, causing performance degradation in cross-platform deployment scenarios.
motivation: Efficient deployment of deep neural networks on diverse hardware requires fast tensor program search; current learned cost model-driven approaches are a computational bottleneck that limits the practical speed of autotuning frameworks like TVM.
method: Pruner introduces a 'Draft-then-Verify' exploration mechanism: a fast Symbol-based Analyzer (draft model) rapidly screens a large pool of schedule candidates using lightweight symbolic analysis, producing a small set of promising drafts. The expensive learned cost model then verifies only these filtered candidates. MoA-Pruner extends this with a Momentum online Adaptation strategy that uses momentum-based gradient updates to adapt the cost model incrementally to new hardware platforms during the tuning process itself, addressing cross-platform unawareness without full retraining.
key_novelty: A two-stage Draft-then-Verify exploration that pairs a cheap symbolic pre-filter with an accurate learned cost model, drastically reducing the number of expensive model evaluations needed per search step.
contributions: Identification and analysis of cross-platform online unawareness as a failure mode of learned cost models in tensor program tuning.
Pruner's Draft-then-Verify mechanism using a Symbol-based Analyzer to pre-screen candidates before invoking the learned cost model.
MoA-Pruner's Momentum online Adaptation strategy for cross-platform cost model adaptation without offline retraining.
Empirical demonstration of significant speedup in schedule search compared to standard TVM-style cost model-only exploration.

metrics.other: search time reduction not quantified in abstract; hours-to-days improvement claimed

limitations: The Symbol-based Analyzer may miss promising candidates filtered out before the learned model, and adaptation accuracy for very different architectures is not characterized from the abstract.
